<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 39:13">Targ. Job XXXIX, 13</cite>.
<cite ref="Onkelos Deuteronomy 4:17">Targ. O. Deut. IV, 17</cite> (ed. Berl. <cite ref="C01197"><he>גַּפָּא</he></cite>, v. Berl. Targ. O. II, p. 50); a. e.—
B. Bath. 73ᵇ דלי ג׳ (Rashbam דליא לי גדנפא, Ms. O. גפא, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 40) lifted (towards me) a wing.—Trnsf. bird; feather, plumage.
<cite ref="Ketubot 105b:10">Keth. 105ᵇ</cite> <he>פרח ג׳ וכ׳</he> a bird flew on his head.
<cite ref="Gittin 86a:3">Gitt. 86ᵃ</cite> <he>בג׳ דאווזא</he> with a goose feather; <cite ref="Avodah Zarah 28a">Ab. Zar. 28ᵃ</cite>.

<cite ref="Chullin 46b:2">Ḥull. 46ᵇ</cite> we put on it <he>ג׳ או רוקא</he> a feather or some spittle.—Pl. <cite ref="C00241"><he>גַּדְפִין</he></cite>, <cite ref="C00241"><he>גַּדְפֵי</he></cite> (<he>גִּי׳</he>).
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 38:13">Targ. Job XXXVIII, 13</cite> borders of the earth.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Genesis 1:21">Targ. Y. Gen. I, 21</cite>; a. e.—B. Bath. l. c. <he>דשמטי גַדְפַיְיהוּ וכ׳</he> whose feathers fell out on account of their fatness.
<cite ref="Chullin 31a:1">Ḥull. 31ᵃ</cite> we see <he>גידפי דמיפרמי</he> that the rims of the cut throat stand apart (Rashi: that the plumage of the throat is cut through).
